polityNote: Russian Empire (Siberia and the Far East) to 1917-11-06 (Provisional Government from March 1917). Amur lands Russian from the Aigun treaty (1858), Ussuri lands from Peking (1860), all Sakhalin from 1875, southern Sakhalin Japanese from 1905; Uryankhai a protectorate from 1914. Old Style decree dates converted to Gregorian (+12 days in the 19th century, +13 from 1900-03-01 O.S.). Scope extended back to the Siberian governorate (29 Dec 1708): no Siberian first-level unit before 1822 is a union of 1897 uyezds (southern fortified lines through 1897 steppe uyezds, the Gorbitsa line inside Nerchinsk-Zavodsk uyezd, the 1822 re-cut of Kansk and Achinsk okrugs); Qing and unadministered lands are named outside until the treaties.

unresolved.what: Tobolsk governorate before the 1887 transfer of Yudinskaya volost
unresolved.why: Until 1887 Tyukalinsk (earlier Omsk) okrug held Yudinskaya volost, which lies inside the 1897 Kainsk uyezd atom (Tomsk group); before that Omsk oblast 1822–1838 and the 1868 loss of Omsk also moved the outer line. Before 1822 the same land lay in the Siberian governorate (18 Dec 1708 O.S.; with Vyatka and Solikamsk provinces to 1727, Iset province 1737–1744), the Tobolsk namestnichestvo (19 Jan 1782 O.S., Tobolsk and Tomsk oblasts) and the Kolyvan oblast/namestnichestvo (1779/1783–1796), the Tobolsk governorate of 1796–1804 (sixteen uyezds from Berezov to Kuznetsk, Semipalatinsk, Krasnoyarsk and Turukhansk) and the Tobolsk and Tomsk governorates of 26 Feb 1804 O.S. Each ran its southern line along the fortified lines — the Ishim line was the southern border of Kurgan, Ishim and Omsk uyezds — and held Omsk, Semipalatinsk and Ust-Kamenogorsk with lands that in 1897 are parts of Akmola and Semipalatinsk uyezds; the Altai south of the Chuya was Qing until the 1864 Chuguchak protocol; and the Tobolsk–Tomsk line of 1804 ran through the later Kainsk and Tyukalinsk lands (Yudinskaya volost, below). No 18th- or early 19th-century unit of western Siberia is a union of 1897 uyezds.

unresolved.why: Until 1851 the governorate also contained Verkhneudinsk and Nerchinsk okrugs, whose eastern edge was the Nerchinsk-treaty line (Gorbitsa), not the 1897 Transbaikal line. Before 1822 the land lay in Irkutsk province (26 Nov 1724 O.S.) of the Siberian governorate, the Irkutsk governorate (1764), the Irkutsk namestnichestvo (6 Mar 1783 O.S.; Irkutsk, Nerchinsk, Yakutsk and Okhotsk oblasts) and the Irkutsk governorate of 1796–1822 — one unit holding the Irkutsk, Transbaikal and Yakutsk lands and (to 1803/1805) Okhotsk and Kamchatka. Its eastern land line was the Nerchinsk-treaty line on the Gorbitsa, inside the 1897 Nerchinsk-Zavodsk uyezd; its Uda lands reached country the treaty left undetermined; and its western line with Tomsk governorate ran through the later Kansk okrug (formed 1822 from parts of Krasnoyarsk and Yeniseysk uyezds and the Ilanskaya and Biryusinskaya volosts of Nizhneudinsk uyezd). So it is not a union of 1897 uyezds; Yakutsk oblast (taken out of the governorate in 1805 by one account) held the Uda lands until 1857 (see the Yakutsk entry).

unresolved.what: Yeniseysk governorate after the Uryankhai protectorate
unresolved.why: Sources disagree whether the Uryankhai protectorate (not annexed; political affairs under the Irkutsk governor-general) became part of the governorate; its extent was never demarcated, so the governorate territory in this window is unsettled.

unresolved.what: Uryankhai krai under the Russian protectorate
unresolved.why: A protectorate, not formally annexed; whether it was part of Yeniseysk governorate is disputed, and its boundary with Mongolia was never demarcated.

unresolved.what: Yeniseysk lands before the Yeniseysk governorate
unresolved.why: Yeniseysk province (1724) of the Siberian governorate, from 1764 in Irkutsk governorate; in 1782–1796 split between the Tobolsk namestnichestvo (Yeniseysk, Achinsk, Turukhansk in Tomsk oblast), the Kolyvan namestnichestvo (Krasnoyarsk) and Irkutsk; 1797–1804 in Tobolsk governorate and 1804–1822 in Tomsk governorate, while Nizhneudinsk lands west of the Biryusa were in Irkutsk. The 1822 statute made Achinsk okrug from parts of Krasnoyarsk, Yeniseysk and Tomsk uyezds and Kansk okrug from Krasnoyarsk, Yeniseysk and Nizhneudinsk lands, so the earlier lines run through 1897 uyezds.
unresolved.needs: the pre-1822 uyezd lines of Krasnoyarsk, Yeniseysk, Achinsk and Nizhneudinsk as atoms

unresolved.what: Okhotsk, Uda, Gizhiga, Kamchatka, Anadyr and Commander lands before 1875
unresolved.why: Kamchatka/Okhotsk units with other lines before 1856; Ussuri lands Qing until Aigun 1858 / Peking 1860; Sakhalin an undivided Russo-Japanese condominium (Shimoda 1855) to 1875, so the Primorskaya share of it has no line. Before 1856: Okhotsk oblast of the Irkutsk namestnichestvo (2 Mar 1783: Aklan, Gizhiga, Nizhnekamchatsk, Okhotsk uyezds); Gizhiga and Kamchatka uyezds made a Kamchatka oblast on 11 Aug 1803; Okhotsk oblast abolished 22 Apr 1805 into Irkutsk governorate; the Uda lands belonged to Yakutsk oblast until 1857; the Commander Islands were settled and run by the Russian-American Company; the Chukchi of the Anadyr were not under ordinary administration. None of these units has an attested line equal to 1897 okrug lines (Anadyr okrug was cut from Gizhiga only in 1888).
unresolved.needs: no atom set can carry the condominium

unresolved.what: Ussuri and lower-Amur lands between the Aigun treaty and 1875
unresolved.why: Left bank of the Amur Russian from Aigun (1858), the Ussuri lands in joint possession until the Peking treaty of 2 (14) Nov 1860; Primorskaya oblast held them with Sakhalin as a condominium (Shimoda 1855) until 1875, so the oblast has no line before 1875.

unresolved.why: Russian posts from 1853; the Shimoda treaty of 1855 left the island undivided between Russia and Japan until the Treaty of St Petersburg (ratifications 22 Aug 1875); the Russian share has no line.
